# Volume 2 — II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

The following afternoon, Nell made a trip by car to Delford to go shopping, accompanied by Isolde Pembroke. Being an official member of the Improvement Society, Isolde joined the other girl in speaking of almost nothing besides it during the entire journey to Delford and their return.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0000 }

“As soon as we begin, our topmost priority should be giving that hall a coat of paint,” Isolde remarked while they passed the Brierley hall, an unsettled structure looking quite run-down in a tree-filled dale, encircled everywhere by looming spruce trees. “The sight of it is shameful, so we need to deal with it prior to attempting to make Mr. Levi Boulder demolish his home. Father believes our efforts there are doomed to fail . . . Levi Gammon lacks the generosity to devote the necessary time.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0001 }

“Maybe he will allow the boys to dismantle it if they give their word to carry the planks away and chop them into kindling for him,” Nell remarked with optimism. “It is necessary that we do as much as possible and be satisfied to advance gradually in the beginning. Expecting to make all things better right away is impossible. Naturally, our initial step must be to cultivate public opinion.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0002 }

While Isolde lacked a clear understanding of what educating public sentiment entailed, it sounded grand, and the prospect of joining an organization with such a purpose filled her with a sense of pride.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0003 }

“I hit upon a plan yesterday evening that we might carry out, Nell. Are you aware of that triangular plot of land located where the roads coming from Delford, Stonebridge, and Pale Sands intersect? Young spruce have completely covered it; however, would it not be pleasant if they were entirely removed, leaving only the two or three birch trees growing there?”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0004 }

“How wonderful,” Nell concurred cheerfully. “Also, ensure a country-style bench is placed beneath the birch trees. Then, upon the arrival of spring, a plot for blossoms must be fashioned right in the center so we can set out geraniums.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0005 }

“Yes; but we must figure out a method to make old Mrs. Hiram Mott prevent her cow from roaming the road, otherwise it will consume all our geraniums,” Isolde chuckled. “I am starting to comprehend your concept of cultivating public opinion, Nell. Look at the former Gammon place over there. Have you ever beheld such a dilapidated structure? Plus, it sits immediately adjacent to the road. A neglected home missing its windowpanes continually reminds me of a corpse whose eyes have been pecked out.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0006 }

“I believe that a dilapidated, abandoned dwelling is a deeply mournful view,” Nell remarked in a daydreaming manner. “To my mind, it appears to constantly ponder its former days and grieve over its past happiness. According to Thirza, a big family grew up inside that aged home a long time back, and it used to be a genuinely lovely spot, featuring an exquisite garden and climbing roses covering it entirely. Little boys and girls, along with mirth and music, filled it completely; yet today it stands vacant, visited by no occupant except the blowing breeze. Its sense of isolation and grief must be so profound! It may be that every one of them returns when the moon shines . . . the spirits of those young boys and girls from days gone by, as well as the roses and the music . . . so that briefly, the ancient dwelling is able to imagine itself youthful and glad once more.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0007 }

Isolde shook her head.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0008 }

“I do not picture things of that nature regarding locations anymore, Nell. Have you forgotten how angry mother and Thirza got when we pictured ghosts inside the Whispering Wood? Even now I am unable to walk past that shrub at night with ease; and were I to start picturing such matters concerning the old Gammon residence, I would likewise be terrified to walk by it. Furthermore, those youths have not died. Every one of them has reached adulthood and is thriving . . . with one working as a butcher. And in any case, blossoms and melodies could not possess ghosts.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0009 }

A quiet sigh was stifled by Nell. Isolde was dearly loved by her, and they had constantly been solid companions. However, she had discovered long before that she was required to travel unaccompanied whenever she roamed into the domain of imagination. The road leading there was an entranced trail upon which she could not be pursued by even those closest to her heart.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0010 }

A rainstorm with thunder arose during the time the girls spent at Delford; nevertheless, it was brief, and there was great pleasure in the journey back, passing along roads where the tree branches held gleaming drops of rain and through small wooded hollows where aromatic scents arose from the soaked ferns. Yet, at the exact moment they made the turn onto the Abernethy road, a sight met Nell’s eyes that ruined the scenic charm of her surroundings.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0011 }

Off to their right, Mr. Pettifer’s wide, grey-green expanse of late oats stretched out, soaked and thick; and right in the center of it, submerged up to her smooth flanks in the rich crop, and placidly blinking at them across the surrounding stalks, stood a Jersey cow!
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0012 }

Releasing her hold on the reins, Nell rose to her feet with a firm setting of her mouth that spelled trouble for the thieving beast. Without uttering a single word, she agilely clambered down past the wheels and darted over the fence ere Isolde grasped the situation.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0013 }

“Nell, return,” screamed the second woman, the moment she regained the ability to speak. “In that damp wheat, your gown will be ruined . . . destroyed. My words aren't reaching her! Oh well, extracting that bovine on her own is impossible for her. Naturally, I have to go render assistance.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0014 }

Nell was rushing through the grain as if she were insane. Isolde leaped down with agility, fastened the horse firmly to a post, flipped the hem of her lovely gingham gown above her shoulders, climbed onto the fence, and began chasing after her agitated companion. She was able to run at a higher speed than Nell, who was restricted by her heavy and soaked skirt, and she quickly caught up with her. In their wake, they left a track that would cause Mr. Pettifer immense grief whenever he happened to spot it.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0015 }

“Nell, please stop, for goodness’ sake,” gasped exhausted Isolde. “I have no breath left, and your clothes are completely soaked.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0016 }

“I have . . . to move . . . that cow . . . away . . . prior to . . . Mr. Pettifer . . . spotting her,” wheezed Nell. “It doesn’t . . . matter . . . if I . . . drown . . . provided we . . . are able . . . to just . . . accomplish that.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0017 }

Yet the Jersey cow seemed to find no valid cause to be hurried away from her rich feeding spot. Hardly had the pair of out-of-breath girls approached her when she spun around and sprinted straight toward the far corner of the pasture.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0018 }

“Intercept her,” Isolde heard Nell screech, urging, “run, Isolde, run.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0019 }

Isolde certainly took off at a run. Nell attempted to do the same, while that malicious Jersey tore about the pasture as though a demon controlled her. In her own mind, Isolde believed the cow actually was. A good ten minutes passed before they managed to block her path and force her through the opening in the corner that led onto the Abernethy lane.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0020 }

It cannot be disputed that, at that exact instant, Nell possessed a disposition that was far from sweet. Furthermore, her mood was not calmed in any way by the sight of a carriage stopped right beside the lane, which carried Mr. Shearer of Delford along with his son, each displaying a wide grin.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0021 }

“I suppose it would have been wiser for you to sell me that cow when I was looking to purchase her last week, Nell,” Mr. Shearer laughed softly.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0022 }

“If you desire her, I will sell her to you right away,” declared her disheveled and flushed master. “She can be yours at this precise moment.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0023 }

“Agreed. I am going to pay you twenty for her like my previous offer, and Saul right beside me is able to take her immediately to Delford. The rest of the shipment tonight will include her when going to town. A Jersey cow is desired by Mr. Reed of Brighton.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0024 }

A short five minutes afterward, Saul Shearer paraded down the road alongside the Jersey cow, whereas impulsive Nell traveled down the lane to Grey Shutters carrying her twenty dollars.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0025 }

“What is Thirza going to say?” Isolde inquired.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0026 }

“Oh, she will not mind. Dolly belonged to me personally, and her sale at the auction would probably not yield over twenty dollars. But goodness me, should Mr. Pettifer spot that grain, he is going to realize she got in a second time, right after I solemnly promised him I would prevent it! Indeed, this experience showed me I should not make solemn promises concerning cows. Any cow capable of clearing or smashing the fence around our milk-pen is not trustworthy in any place.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0027 }

Thirza’s trip down to Mrs. Sowerby’s ended with her learning every detail regarding the sale and transfer of Dolly, because the majority of the deal had been witnessed by Mrs. Sowerby from her window, with her inferring the remaining parts.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0028 }

“Although you handle affairs in a terribly impulsive manner, Nell, I guess her departure is for the best. Nevertheless, I fail to understand how she escaped the pen. Some of the boards must have been kicked loose by her.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0029 }

“It did not occur to me to search,” Nell remarked, “however I am going to check right away. Martin has still not returned. Maybe additional aunts of his have passed away. In my mind, it resembles the situation with Mr. Peter Mott and the octogenarians. A few nights ago, Mrs. Mott was perusing a paper and remarked to Mr. Mott, ‘It says in this place that yet another octogenarian has passed away recently. Peter, what constitutes an octogenarian?’ And Mr. Mott replied that he was uncertain, though they had to be extremely frail beings, because the only time anyone ever spoke of them was when they were passing away. Martin’s aunts are just like that.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0030 }

“Martin is merely identical to all those other Frenchmen,” Thirza remarked with revulsion. “They cannot be relied upon for even one day.” As Thirza inspected the items Nell bought in Delford, a piercing scream echoed from the barnyard. Within a minute, Nell burst into the kitchen, clutching her hands in distress.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0031 }

“Nell Harcourt, what is wrong this time?”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0032 }

“Oh, Thirza, what am I going to do? It is awful. And I am entirely to blame. Oh, is there any chance I will learn to pause and think a bit prior to acting recklessly? I was always warned by Mrs. Sowerby that I’d commit some terrible act eventually, and now it has happened!”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0033 }

“What have you done, Nell? You really are the most infuriating girl!”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0034 }

“Mr. Pettifer’s Jersey cow . . . which Mr. Bell sold to him previously . . . has been purchased by Mr. Shearer! Right now, Dolly stands outside within the milking pen.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0035 }

“Nell Harcourt, are you dreaming?”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0036 }

“How I want that to be true. No dreaming is involved, even if it closely resembles a bad dream. Furthermore, the cow belonging to Mr. Pettifer has reached Port Marlow already. Oh, Thirza, my belief was that I had stopped causing trouble for myself, yet now I find myself in the most dreadful trouble of my entire existence. What course is open to me?”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0037 }

“Do? There is no action to take, child, other than going to speak with Mr. Pettifer regarding the matter. Should he refuse the cash, we are able to propose swapping our Jersey with him instead. Our cow matches his in quality.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0038 }

“However, I’m certain he’ll be extremely annoyed and unpleasant regarding it,” Nell lamented.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0039 }

“I imagine that he will. A short-tempered kind of fellow appears to be what he is. If it pleases you, I will make my way over and clarify matters to him.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0040 }

“Certainly not, my stinginess does not go that far,” Nell cried out. “Because the blame lies entirely with me, I will definitely not permit you to be punished in my place. Going myself is what I will do, and I will do it immediately. Since the humiliation will be dreadful, getting it finished quickly is preferable.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0041 }

Unhappy Nell retrieved her twenty dollars along with her hat, and as she was leaving, her eyes chanced to fall through the pantry’s unclosed door. Resting upon the table was a nut cake that she had made earlier that day . . . an especially delicious creation coated in pink frosting and decorated with walnuts. Nell’s plan was to serve it on Friday night, when the young people of Brierley were scheduled to gather at Grey Shutters for the purpose of founding the Improvement Society. Yet how did they measure up to Mr. Pettifer, who had every right to be angry? Nell reasoned that such a cake should melt the heart of any man, particularly someone forced to prepare his own meals, so she quickly placed it inside a box. It would serve as a peace offering when she presented it to Mr. Pettifer.
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0042 }

“Provided he grants me the opportunity to speak whatsoever,” she reflected with regret while scaling the lane fence and beginning her route across the fields, which gleamed gold beneath the gentle glow of the hazy August dusk. “I truly comprehend at present the sensations of those being escorted to their death.”
{: #nw-v02-c02-p0043 }
